themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 185 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 33.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 458% spike (z-score: 7.14)—suggesting acute pavement failure or pothole formation across Sunnyside/Woodside that demands immediate investigation into whether weather, deferred maintenance, or construction activity is the culprit.
evidence: 185 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 33.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
458% increase representing z-score of 7.14 (high statistical significance)
633 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (110 new buildings, 423 alterations) suggesting active construction disruption
reporting_angles: Map the spatial distribution of this week's complaints—are they concentrated on specific avenues or tied to active construction sites?
Interview NYC DOT about emergency repair crews and whether they're responding to the spike or backlogged

themes_detail.label: Encampment Proliferation
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 21 THIS WEEK against a baseline of 4.5 per week over 8 weeks—a 367% spike (z-score: 4.41)—indicating a rapid concentration of unsheltered populations or visible encampments that may signal a wider homelessness crisis or service gap in the district.
evidence: 21 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly baseline (8-week average)
367% increase representing z-score of 4.41 (high statistical significance)
No recent council constituent cases or local news mentions, suggesting this may be underreported
reporting_angles: Locate the encampments 311 complaints are identifying—are they near transit hubs, parks, or residential blocks?
Interview NYC Department of Homeless Services about whether Sunnyside/Woodside is experiencing displacement from other neighborhoods or a capacity issue at local shelters

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints reached 5 exactly 3 weeks ago (versus a baseline of 0.1 per week)—a 3900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—pointing to sudden commercial or political advertising saturation, graffiti, or bill-posting that warrants investigation into whether enforcement is failing or a campaign is targeting the district.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
3900% increase representing z-score of 14.74 (extremely high statistical significance)
Spike occurred 3 weeks ago, not this week—older than other emerging signals
reporting_angles: Pull photos from 311 complaints to identify what was posted and whether it's political, commercial, or gang-related
Check with NYC Department of Sanitation enforcement on what they issued violations for in that period

themes_detail.label: Tree Canopy & Safety Requests
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests and site safety complaints each spiked to 3 complaints THIS WEEK (versus baselines of 0.1 per week)—both 2300% increases (z-scores: 8.69)—suggesting residents perceive both environmental and structural deficiencies that may reflect deferred park or streetscape maintenance.
evidence: 3 new tree requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline; 3 site safety complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline
Both spikes represent 2300% increases with z-scores of 8.69 (high statistical significance)
Community board budget requests include repeated pleas for new/expanded parks and park amenities (unsolved, year-over-year)
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about tree canopy cover and planting schedules in CD 402 versus citywide benchmarks
Cross-reference site safety complaints with DOB permit data to determine whether active construction sites are unsafe

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Animal Infestation Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints peaked at 12 three weeks ago (versus a baseline of 3.4 per week)—a 256% spike—and unsanitary animal on private property complaints hit 4 last week (versus 0.2 baseline)—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—indicating an uncontrolled pest problem that may reflect sanitation service gaps or construction-related disruption.
evidence: 12 rodent complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.4 weekly baseline (256% increase, z-score: 7.08)
4 unsanitary animal complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
Spikes are 1-3 weeks old, not this week—slower-emerging than street/encampment signals
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene on whether a particular neighborhood block or waste transfer facility is causing the spike
Speak with residents on affected blocks about whether construction, restaurant violations, or inadequate sanitation pickup is driving rodents
